To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nucleon structure function ratios are not universal and that the EMC effect is a consequence of a change of quark distribution inside the nucleon.

(i) the EMC effect, i.e. the nuclear modification of nucleon structure, is a genuine nuclear effect and not an artifact of the nuclear environment; (ii) the EMC effect is a function of the nuclear environment, in particular, of the nuclear binding energy and the density of nuclear matter.

the EMC effect is not a simple scaling effect and that it is not a single effect, but rather that the EMC effect has to be understood as a collection of several effects, some of which have been identified.

the nucleon structure is the same in all nuclei, and that the EMC effect is due to the nuclear binding and the Fermi motion of nucleons.

the BCDMS spectrometers can be upgraded to measure the structure functions of nuclei with high statistics and good resolution in the region ofx≳0·6 and Q2>50 GeV2, which is the most interesting region for the EMC effect.

it would be possible to measure the EMC effect in a wide range of nuclei with atomic numbers from 2 to about 207, and that the measurements of the EMC effect in the range ofx≈0.4–0.6 are of particular interest.
